definition: The General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (GPAI CoP) is a compliance tool released by the European Commission on 10 July 2025 to support compliance with the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act).
details: It provides operational guidance for providers of general-purpose AI models, particularly in relation to Articles 53 and 55 of the AI Act, which entered into application on 2 August 2025. The Code is organised into three chapters (Transparency, Copyright, and Safety and Security) and outlines how providers can meet the Act's relevant obligations. Although non-binding, providers can rely on adherence to the Code, meaning that EU regulators will assume that providers following the Code meet the corresponding legal requirements of the AI Act. As such, signatories to the Code will benefit from reduced administrative burdens and increased legal certainty compared to providers that prove compliance in other ways. While adherence to the Code is voluntary, compliance with the AI Act is not.

explainer.lead: The General-Purpose AI Code of Practice is a voluntary guide from the European Commission for meeting parts of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act. It gives AI model providers a clearer route to compliance, with less administrative work and greater legal certainty for those who follow it.

tiers.eli5: Think of the AI Act as a rulebook and this Code as a guidebook showing how to follow some of its rules. AI companies do not have to use the guidebook, but regulators will assume that companies following it are meeting the matching rules. The guidebook is optional; obeying the law is not.
tiers.practitioner: Engineering and compliance teams can use the Code’s Transparency, Copyright, and Safety and Security chapters to organise work relevant to Articles 53 and 55 of the AI Act. Following the Code can reduce administrative burden, but signing it does not make the underlying legal obligations optional. Providers may instead demonstrate compliance through other routes.
tiers.paperLevel: The GPAI Code of Practice is non-binding operational guidance, released by the European Commission on 10 July 2025, for providers of general-purpose AI models subject to relevant AI Act obligations, particularly Articles 53 and 55. Regulatory adherence can be expressed as: provider follows Code -> regulators assume corresponding AI Act requirements are met. Its scope is organised into Transparency, Copyright, and Safety and Security, and adherence is only one possible way to prove compliance.

EU regulators: assume adhering providers meet corresponding requirements.

explainer.outcome: The Code creates a voluntary compliance route for relevant general-purpose AI model obligations. Providers that follow it benefit from a regulatory assumption of compliance, while other providers can prove compliance in different ways.
explainer.whyItMatters: It turns parts of the AI Act into practical guidance and makes one compliance route more predictable. It also preserves a clear distinction between voluntary adherence to the Code and mandatory compliance with the Act.
